subject: Re: Delivery format for selective preservation packet for AcmeHealth audit export
messages:
From: Emma Liu <emma.liu@acmehealth.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@acmehealth.com
Date: 2028-10-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Selective preservation packet format and delivery

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking this. For Acme's upcoming SIG review and a parallel SOC2 spot-check we need a tenant-scoped preservation export for a limited window (2028-07-01 to 2028-07-14). Our requirements:
- Only session traces and debug logs tied to tenant id ACME-9987 (no other tenant data).
- PII redaction: full names, email addresses, phone numbers must be permanently redacted; system identifiers (request ids, session ids) should be preserved.
- Keystore evidence: metadata showing key IDs used to encrypt logs and the rotation history for July 2028.
- A signed manifest listing files, SHA256 checksums, and row counts.
- Delivery via pre-signed S3 URL or an encrypted evidence bundle.

Can you confirm the exact file formats you can provide (CSV/JSONL/NDJSON), how redaction will be applied (mask vs pseudonymize), and an estimated delivery date? We will need a short acceptance checklist so our compliance team can validate.

I attached a template of fields we expect (acme_preservation_fields_template.csv).

Best,
Emma
Data Privacy Ops — Acme Health

From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@acmehealth.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Selective preservation packet format and delivery

Emma — thanks for the clear template. Short answers up front: we can deliver NDJSON for events, a CSV manifest with checksums, and an encrypted tarball for keystore metadata. We will apply permanent redaction (one-way masking) for PII by default; we can provide optional reversible pseudonymization if you have a signed Data Processing Addendum that permits a reversible mapping for the audit window.

Proposed deliverables and formats:
- events_ACME-9987_20280701-20280714.ndjson (each line is an event JSON; PII keys removed/masked)
- manifest_acme_preservation_v1.csv (filename, sha256, rows, generator-version)
- keystore_metadata_july2028.json.gz (encrypted, includes key IDs + rotation timestamps)
- signature: evidence_tarball_signature.asc (GPG detached signature over the tarball)

Acceptance criteria we suggest for your team:
1) File list matches manifest exactly.
2) SHA256 checksums validate.
3) Sample of 10 events (we will provide redacted and original-field-indexed examples) pass your PII check.
4) Keystore metadata contains rotation entries covering 2028-07-01..2028-07-31.

Timeline: initial package draft by 2028-10-25 EOD PST, final signed delivery by 2028-10-27 after your acceptance check. If you prefer reversible pseudonymization instead of masking we'll need written scope and a 48-hour alignment call.

I'll have Priyom produce the snapshot and Mina prepare the keystore export; copying them on this thread.

Thanks,
Jonas
Director, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Emma Liu <emma.liu@acmehealth.com>
Cc: mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-23T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Selective preservation packet format and delivery

Adding the technical approach so expectations line up. Key points:
- Snapshot generation: we'll run a tenant-scoped extraction job (job id: SNAP-ACME-9987-20281023) that streams events into NDJSON and applies redaction hooks at export time. Redaction implementation: remove values for keys matching name/email/phone and replace with static tokens (e.g., [REDACTED_EMAIL]). This is irreversible in the export; reversible pseudonyms would require creating a separate mapping table stored encrypted and only shared under your data-handling agreement.
- Keystore metadata: we will include a minimal, non-secret manifest with key IDs, algorithm, and rotation timestamps. We will not share private key material. The metadata file will be signed and GPG-encrypted for transport.
- Checksums: sha256sum over each file, then included in CSV manifest. We will generate the manifest using our deterministic filename schema so validation is straightforward.
- Evidence packaging: tar.gz of files, then GPG sign the tar.gz. For transfer we can either put tar.gz on an S3 bucket with a 7-day presigned URL or push to your secure intake URL (if you provide).

Sample commands we will use (internal runbook refs):
- export job: ./infra/tools/export_snapshot --tenant ACME-9987 --start 2028-07-01 --end 2028-07-14 --out events_ACME-9987.ndjson --redact-profile PII-MASK
- manifest generation: ./infra/tools/mk_manifest --dir ./out --algo sha256 > manifest_acme_preservation_v1.csv

I'll start the export 2028-10-24 02:00 UTC to avoid peak serving windows. ETA for draft package: 2028-10-25 02:00 UTC.

-Priyom
Staff Engineer, Platform Tools

From: Emma Liu <emma.liu@acmehealth.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@acmehealth.com
Date: 2028-10-24T10:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Selective preservation packet format and delivery

Thanks — that looks good. Quick clarifications before you run:
1) The PII-MASK profile: can you confirm email masking replaces local-part with a stable token per email (i.e., same input email maps to same token) or is it full irreversible redaction? For our audit we prefer stable pseudonymization so we can follow a user across events without seeing the raw email.
2) Keystore metadata: please include the KMS key alias as used within Redwood; we need the alias to reconcile with our security team.
3) Can you include a small sample (10 events) in the draft package that demonstrates the masking approach and a separate companion file that lists the keys removed (only keys, not values)?

If stable pseudonymization requires extra approvals, we can sign a narrow use addendum. Please flag that in the draft.

—Emma

Date: 2028-10-24T16:54:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Selective preservation packet format and delivery

Emma — quick confirmation and next steps:
- We can support stable pseudonymization for emails (deterministic HMAC with per-tenant salt) but will need a signed addendum that limits use to your compliance review and specifies deletion of the mapping after 30 days. I attached a one-page scope addendum (selective_snapshot_readme.pdf) and the manifest template (acme_preservation_manifest_v1.csv) to this thread.
- Mina will prepare the keystore metadata and include the KMS aliases.
- We will produce the draft package by 2028-10-25 02:00 UTC containing: NDJSON (10-event sample + full export), manifest CSV, keystore metadata (encrypted), and signature.
- Final signed delivery by 2028-10-27 after your acceptance checklist is completed.

Next steps for Acme: reply to this thread with either (A) written approval for reversible pseudonymization limited to the audit (we will route our legal doc), or (B) confirmation to proceed with irreversible masking. If we don't hear back by EOD 2028-10-24 PST we'll proceed with irreversible masking to avoid delays.

Thanks everyone — we aim for minimal disruption to your production tenant.

Jonas
Director, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference
